d.a: DISTRIBUTION: A single collection, from ‘ Au‘Au Channel, Maui, Hawai‘i, USA; mesophotic depth of 104 m. Morphology and ecology Blades single or clustered, 1 – 6 cm in height, 1 – 8 cm wide, lobed with broadly crenate margins (Fig. 14). Blades in cross section uniformly 40 – 80 µm thick. Stipe and mode of attachment to substrate not observed. The medulla consisting primarily of sparse filaments and stellate cells with central bodies ranging from 5 – 10 µm wide by 1 – 3 µm high, and elongate, slender arms (4 – 6 in number) that are 2 – 3 µm wide by 15 – 50 µm long (Fig. 15). Surface view of outer cortical ovoid cells 1 – 3 µm wide by 5 – 10 µm high (Fig. 16). Tetrasporangial and gametangial reproduction not observed. Although mode of attachment of blades was not identified, parts of blades were found entwined with species of mounding, prostrate species of Halimeda J. V. Lamouroux, which are abundant in the ‘ Au‘Au Channel, Maui (see Spalding et al. 2019, fig. 29.1 b). Blades of C. haukoaweo are only documented in the MHI in the ‘ Au‘Au Channel, Maui at 104 m depth.
